assessment.nobel_worthiness: Pd-catalyzed C-N cross-coupling turned aryl amine construction from a harsh, substrate-limited exercise into a routine, general transformation. Ligand design (bulky phosphines, biaryl phosphines) is a clear chemical advance, and the reaction is used daily in pharmaceutical and materials synthesis. It is the clearest case of a general method that changed how chemists build bonds, and it follows naturally from the 2010 cross-coupling prize.
assessment.attribution: Buchwald and Hartwig independently developed the catalytic, ligand-controlled, broadly applicable versions and are the decisive pair. Kosugi's earlier tin-amide coupling and Migita-type precedent are real but were not general or practical; this is an allocation question I would raise but not resolve in favor of a third laureate.
assessment.maturity: Four decades of use, thousands of industrial applications, mechanism well understood. Fully mature and timely.
uncertainties: Weight to give Kosugi's 1983 precedent versus the later general catalytic systems; I rely on my own recollection of the history rather than verification.
Overlap with the 2010 cross-coupling prize could be read as a prior recognition of the same concept.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Visible-light photoredox catalysis opened radical and single-electron pathways under mild conditions, enabling bond constructions that were impractical by two-electron chemistry, and it has been widely adopted in medicinal chemistry and late-stage functionalization. The conceptual shift is new chemistry, not just a new reagent.
assessment.attribution: The 2008 to 2009 papers of MacMillan (with Nicewicz), Yoon and Stephenson launched the field; König, Fukuzumi, Melchiorre and Nicewicz also have strong claims. MacMillan already shares the 2021 prize, which complicates a fair configuration and may favor others.
assessment.maturity: Fifteen-plus years of broad independent adoption, industrial and flow applications; mature though still expanding.
uncertainties: MacMillan was recognized in 2021 for organocatalysis; whether the committee wants to honor him again is doubtful.
Credit is diffuse across at least seven groups and earlier precedents (Kellogg, Fukuzumi, Cano-Yelo and Deronzier).

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Isolation of stable carbenes (imidazolylidenes by Arduengo, phosphino carbenes by Bertrand) overturned the view that carbenes are only transient, and N-heterocyclic carbenes became ubiquitous ligands and organocatalysts, underpinning modern olefin metathesis catalysts and main-group chemistry. Clear, original, lasting.
assessment.attribution: Bertrand's 1988 phosphinocarbene and Arduengo's 1991 crystalline NHC are the decisive discoveries. Nolan, Rovis and Bode represent the later catalytic exploitation rather than the founding discovery, so a two-person prize is natural.
assessment.maturity: Over thirty years of confirmation and heavy adoption; fully mature.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views the prize as honoring the isolation or the downstream ligand and catalysis uses, which would shift the laureate set.
Bertrand's phosphinocarbene and Arduengo's NHC are different classes; I am unsure how cleanly they combine.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Selective C-H functionalization lets chemists treat C-H bonds as functional groups, shortening syntheses and enabling late-stage diversification. Directing-group, ligand-accelerated and template strategies for site selectivity are real chemical advances aligned with efficiency in synthesis.
assessment.attribution: Yu (ligand-enabled and remote meta/para C-H activation) and Sanford (Pd(II/IV) catalysis and directed functionalization) are leading figures; Hartwig (borylation) and Daugulis (directing groups) also have important claims. Allocation is genuinely unresolved and the field is broad.
assessment.maturity: Widely used and increasingly applied in total synthesis and industry, but the field is still evolving and selectivity problems remain; moderately mature.
uncertainties: Whether a coherent single discovery can be defined within so diverse a field.
Hartwig's overlap with B023 and with iridium borylation complicates credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Frustrated Lewis pairs showed that sterically encumbered acid-base pairs activate H2 and other small molecules without metals, opening metal-free hydrogenation catalysis. A conceptually simple and new idea in main-group chemistry.
assessment.attribution: Stephan's 2006 metal-free reversible H2 activation and Erker's related intramolecular systems are the decisive contributions; a two-person prize is natural.
assessment.maturity: Broadly confirmed and extended to many small molecules, but practical impact on synthesis is smaller than for transition-metal catalysis; moderately mature.
uncertainties: Practical scope of FLP hydrogenation relative to established metal catalysts.
Credit to Welch and Stephan versus Erker's earlier related work.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editing converts one base to another without double-strand breaks by pairing evolved deaminases with CRISPR proteins, a chemical-biology design strategy with clinical consequences. From my synthetic vantage, the question is what was new chemically: harnessing nucleobase deamination chemistry with protein evolution.
assessment.attribution: Liu's group led the work (Komor, Gaudelli as lead authors); Nishida and Kondo reported an independent cytidine deaminase fusion. A sole-laureate or Liu-led configuration is plausible, while trainee credit is a standard issue.
assessment.maturity: First clinical applications are emerging and the technology is widely adopted, but long-term safety and therapeutic outcomes are still maturing; possibly slightly premature.
uncertainties: Proximity to the 2020 CRISPR prize and to biology rather than chemistry.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Bergman's 1982 intermolecular oxidative addition of alkane C-H bonds to iridium complexes showed that unreactive alkanes could be cleaved by a metal center, founding the field of C-H activation and inspiring later functionalization chemistry. Conceptually important.
assessment.attribution: Bergman is the clear lead on this specific discovery, with parallel work by Graham; the candidate credits only Bergman, so a single laureate is the supplied option.
assessment.maturity: More than forty years old and extensively confirmed, though stoichiometric alkane activation itself had limited direct synthetic use; very mature, possibly overshadowed by later catalytic C-H work.
uncertainties: The prize might be seen as better directed at catalytic C-H functionalization (B050).
Parallel work by others, such as Graham and Jones, is not credited here and I cannot verify relative priority.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Native chemical ligation enabled chemoselective joining of unprotected peptide fragments and routine chemical synthesis of proteins, including expressed protein ligation for semisynthesis. It is a general, simple solution to a long-standing synthetic problem.
assessment.attribution: Dawson, Muir, Kent and Kent's 1994 paper established NCL; Muir extended it to semisynthesis. Danishefsky, Brik and Liu contributed later refinements and applications, so credit is unresolved.
assessment.maturity: Thirty years of use in protein chemistry and biologics research; mature, though synthetic impact is concentrated in a specialist community.
uncertainties: Whether the 2018 or similar prizes in protein chemistry reduce room for another biomolecular synthesis award.
Allocation among Kent, Dawson, Muir and Danishefsky is not settled.
